BURHAN:v2p287/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p287/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p287/r1.claim: A maṣdar can carry a passive sense: علم is what is known, مبلغهم من العلم means their knowledge, and صنع means something made.
BURHAN:v2p287/r1.anchor: ومجئ المصدر بمعنى المفعول كقوله تعالى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r4.claim: The Prophet is consoled to turn from worldly people indifferent to God's message; God knows who strays or is guided and will give each person their due.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r4.anchor: The Prophet (sws) has been solaced that he should turn away from the slaves to this world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r5.claim: Angels cannot speak or intercede without God's permission; naming them as female and relying on them to evade accountability will not help, for God knows the righteous and wrongdoers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r5.anchor: Not even an angel can open his mouth in the presence of God without His permission

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r4.claim: They attend only to the world's outward form and neither perceive nor desire its deeper reality, though that reality should be their priority; the universe's evident Creator makes a merely playful purpose implausible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r4.anchor: neither do they have access to the reality behind this external form nor do they have any desire for it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r5.claim: The verse's phrasing exposes their narrow-mindedness: temporary pleasures distract them from reality, while timidity and deprivation keep them from pursuing the eternal kingdom to which the Qur'an calls them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r5.anchor: that it is merely their narrow mindedness and meanness that they are lured by its external form and have become indifferent to its reality

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r6.claim: Islahi cites 30:7 to explain this contrast between knowing worldly appearances and neglecting the life to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p57/r6.anchor: This aspect is explained by the following verse of Sūrah al-Rūm:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r1.claim: The closing verse reassures the Prophet and warns worldly-minded people: God knows who strays and who is guided, judges each justly, and will neither let the strayed escape nor withhold aid and mercy from those enduring hardship for His cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p58/r1.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is addressed and told that he should now ignore them; his Lord fully knows those who have deviated from His path as well as those who are rightly guided.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r5.claim: مبلغهم means their limit in knowledge: they know worldly trades, farming, and crafts, as in the verse about knowing only the outward life of this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r5.anchor: مبلغهم: غايتهم ومنتهاهم من العلم، وهو ما تعلقت به علومهم من مكاسب الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r6.claim: After describing their state, God states that He knows the astray and guided and will recompense them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r6.anchor: ولما ذكر ما هم عليه، أخبر تعالى بأنه عالم بالضال والمهتدي، وهو مجازيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r7.claim: He calls ذلك مبلغهم من العلم an aside.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقوله: ذلك مبلغهم من العلم: اعتراض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r8.claim: The author sees no basis for treating it as an aside interrupting فأعرض and إن ربك.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r8.anchor: ولا يظهر هذا الذي يقوله من الاعتراض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r9.claim: One view takes ذلك as pointing to their claim that angels are God’s daughters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r9.anchor: وقيل: ذلك إشارة إلى جعلهم الملائكة بنات الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r10.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r10.claim: He says their judgment is small and their minds foolish: their intellectual limit is preferring this world to the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء: صغر رأيهم وسفه أحلامهم، أي غاية عقولهم ونهاية علومهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes ذلك as referring to conjecture: their utmost intellectual activity is to rely on speculation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r11.anchor: وقيل: ذلك إشارة إلى الظن، أي غاية ما يفعلون أن يأخذوا بالظن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r12.claim: God’s knowledge of the astray and guided consoles the Prophet, who wanted them to believe, while warning unbelievers and promising believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p19/r12.anchor: وقوله: إن ربك هو أعلم في معرض التسلية، إذ كان من خلقه عليه الصلاة والسلام الحرص على إيمانهم

NAHHAS:v4p272/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p272/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v4p272/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says their knowledge goes no further than their associationism, disbelief, and obstinate rejection of what came from God.
NAHHAS:v4p272/r12.anchor: قال ابن زيد ليس لهم علم إلا الذي هم فيه من الشرك والكفر ومكابرتهم

NAHHAS:v4p272/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p272/r13.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v4p272/r13.claim: Another view says this is the limit of their knowledge: they chose the fading adornment and status of worldly life over the lasting reward of the Hereafter.
NAHHAS:v4p272/r13.anchor: وقال غيره ذلك مبلغهم من العلم أنهم آثروا ما يفنى من زينة الدنيا

NAHHAS:v4p272/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p272/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p272/r14.claim: أعلم may mean simply knowing, or keep its comparative sense with an omitted comparison; سبيله is the way of Islam, and those guided are on the true path of Islam in God's prior knowledge.
NAHHAS:v4p272/r14.anchor: يكون أعلم بمعنى عالم ويجوز أن يكون على بابه بالحذف وسبيل الإسلام

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.claim: The second section reproaches Quraysh for idol worship, discusses its roots in ignorance and conjecture, and condemns seeking angels’ intercession.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r14.anchor: The second section (vv. 19–30) reproaches the Quraysh for worshipping idols

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r1.claim: The clearest antecedent for “that” is conjecture: the farthest these people reach in knowledge is reliance on conjecture.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r1.anchor: غاية ما يبلغون به أنهم يأخذون بالظن

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r2.claim: A second possibility is that preferring worldly life is the limit of their knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r2.anchor: إيثار الحياة الدنيا مبلغهم من العلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r3.claim: A third possibility takes “that” to mean the turning away described just before; here “knowledge” means the known thing, the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r3.anchor: وذلك الإعراض غاية ما بلغوه من العلم

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r4.claim: Rāzī describes responses to the Qur’an from highest to lowest: wholehearted acceptance, acceptance of its miracle and following the Messenger, hesitation such as Abū Ṭālib’s, and rejection with blame.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r4.anchor: بعضهم تلقاه بالقبول وانشرح صدره فبلغ الغاية القصوى

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r5.claim: Although one might object that God does not burden beyond capacity and a child or mad person lacks knowledge, Rāzī says their ignorance followed their turning away from remembrance, so it grounds their punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats 53:30 as an interruption; the connected sequence runs from the command to turn away from those who abandon remembrance to God’s knowledge of the astray.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري : { ذلك مبلغهم من العلم } كلام معترض بين كلامين

RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3/r7.claim: Rāzī argues the central statement is needed to explain the command: leave them because this is the utmost they attain; their turning away and preference for the immediate explain their ignorance.

RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r1.claim: First, the Prophet hoped reminders would win more of his people without fighting; God’s knowledge of who is guided or astray means debate should give way to fighting, and removes uncertainty or despair about the outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r1.anchor: علم أنه يؤمن بمجرد الدعاء أحد من المكلفين

RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r2.claim: Second, as in 34:24 and 7:87, opponents claimed guidance despite the Prophet’s proof; he should leave the judgment to God, like litigants before a powerful king who knows the truth.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r2.anchor: وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو فى ضلال مبين

RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r3.claim: Third, the Prophet had endured serious harm hoping they would believe; since they did not, God’s knowledge of misled and guided people assures recompense for evil and good.
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r3.anchor: لله ما في السموات والأرض ليجزي الذين أساؤوا بما عملوا ويجزي الذين أحسنوا

RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p3#2/r4.claim: The pronoun huwa is an ʿimād or faṣl. Though the sentence is complete without it, it prevents a hearer from wondering whether “most knowing” is the predicate or part of a following clause.

RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r1.claim: Rāzī says أَعْلَمُ can mean عالم: God has no equal knower; alternatively it is truly comparative against any hypothetical other knower.

RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r2.claim: علم may take its object directly or with ب; direct attachment can reflect stronger knowledge, a more evident object, required certainty, or greater force of the action.

RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r3.claim: Here أعلم is a noun denoting an action, whose weaker verbal government accounts for the preposition ب before its object.
RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r3.anchor: كما كان المستعمل اسما دالا على فعل ضعف عمله لتعلقه بالمفعول

RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r1.claim: Across these passages, mentioning the astray before the guided threatens the stubborn opponents and consoles the Prophet, since he faces them in each context.
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r1.anchor: فذكرهم أولا تهديدا لهم وتسلية لقلب نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r2.claim: Eternal divine knowledge relates to an event as it actually occurs, without a delay between occurrence and knowledge; no atom escapes God in heaven or earth.
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r2.anchor: فهو أن العلم القديم يتعلق بالمعلوم على ما هو عليه

RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r3.claim: The active participle governs like a verb for a future sense, but not for a past one; hence one says أنا غدا ضارب زيدا, while a past construction requires a finite verb or genitive attachment.
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r3.anchor: اسم الفاعل يعمل عمل الفعل إذا كان بمعنى المستقبل ولا يعمل عمله إذا كان ماضيا

RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r6.claim: This passage uses past ضل because the turning away had occurred and the Prophet had despaired and been told to withdraw; 6:117 uses يضل after the warning that most people would mislead him.
RAZI-FULL:v29p5/r6.anchor: ههنا حصل الضلال في الماضي وتأكد حيث حصل يأس الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمر بالإعراض

STUDYQURAN:53:30/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r1.claim: One reading is that disbelievers look only to worldly matters and are ignorant of religion.
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r1.anchor: The extent of their knowledge can be seen as a reference to the fact that the disbelievers look only to the world and are ignorant of religion (Q)

STUDYQURAN:53:30/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r2.claim: Alternatively, their claims about angels and idols rest only on conjecture, caprice, and desire.
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r2.anchor: or as an indication that their “knowledge,” especially as pertains to the angels and idols mentioned in the preceding verses, derives solely from conjecture, caprice, and their own desires

STUDYQURAN:53:30/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r3.claim: The second sentence recurs in 6:117, appears with minor variation in 68:7, and is also compared with 28:85.
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r3.anchor: The second sentence of this verse is repeated in 6:117, and with minor variation in 68:7 (see also 28:85).

STUDYQURAN:53:30/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r4.claim: Generally, the statement means God knows the final ends of all things.
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r4.anchor: In general it indicates that God knows the final ends of all things

STUDYQURAN:53:30/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r5.claim: In context, God knows the difference between Muslim and pagan beliefs.
STUDYQURAN:53:30/r5.anchor: in this context it also refers to God knowing the difference between the beliefs of the Muslims and that of the pagans.

TAB-FULL:v22p58/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p58/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p58/r1.claim: Their claim that angels are female is the full extent of the unbelievers' knowledge: disbelief, shirk, and conjecture without certain knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v22p58/r1.anchor: بالله، والشرك به على وجه الظن بغير يقين علم

TAB-FULL:v22p58/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p58/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p58/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says their knowledge goes no further than rejecting the Messenger and plotting against what came from God; they are the people of shirk.
TAB-FULL:v22p58/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم}

BURSEVI:v9p196/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r1.claim: Anything that distances a person from God's presence is worldly life; seeking asceticism, piety, disclosures, or miracles for popularity, fame, status, or wealth wastes one's spiritual states and deeds without reward.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r1.anchor: فمن قصد بالزهد والورع والتقى والكشف والكرامات وخوارق العادات قبول الناس والشهرة عندهم وحصول الجاه والمال

BURSEVI:v9p196/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r2.claim: Do not be deceived by apparent unveiling or worldly acclaim: these may be immediate returns, as Iblis's nine thousand years of worship were followed by respite after his disbelief.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r2.anchor: ولا يغترن هذا بحصول بعض الكشوف وإقبال أهل الدنيا عليه فإنه ثمرة عاجلة له

BURSEVI:v9p196/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r3.claim: The author takes dhālika to refer to their desire for worldly life.

BURSEVI:v9p196/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v9p196/r4.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlūm identifies the referent as choosing worldly life over the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r4.anchor: وفي بحرالعلوم أي إرادة الدنيا وإيثارها على الآخرة

BURSEVI:v9p196/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v9p196/r5.claim: Al-Irshād identifies it as what led them to turn away and restrict their desires to worldly life.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r5.anchor: وفي الإرشاد أي ما أداهم إلى ما هم فيه من التولي وقصر الإرادة على الحياة الدنيا

BURSEVI:v9p196/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r6.claim: Mablagh means their limit of knowledge: they scarcely pass beyond worldly concerns to benefit from admonition, and al-ʿilm here includes false conjectural perception.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r6.anchor: لا يكادون يجاوزونه إلى غيره حتى يجديهم الدعوة والإرشاد

BURSEVI:v9p196/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r7.claim: Mablagh is a place or extent noun; the pronoun is plural because min is construed by meaning here, whereas the earlier singular follows its grammatical form.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r7.anchor: فبلغ اسم مكان وجمع الضمير في مبلغهم باعتباره معنى من كما أن أفراده فيما سبق باعتبار لفظها

BURSEVI:v9p196/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r8.claim: The clause interrupts the address to affirm how their ambition is confined to low worldly life; 30:7 similarly says they know the outward side of worldly life but are heedless of the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r8.anchor: والجملة اعتراض مقرر لقصر همتهم على الدنيا الدنية

BURSEVI:v9p196/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v9p196/r9.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says God created nothing more hateful to Him than the world and has not looked toward it since creating it, out of hatred.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r9.anchor: إن الله لم يخلق خلقا هو أبغض إليه من الدنيا وما نظر إليها منذ خلقها بغضا لها رواه أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v9p196/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p196/r10.claim: The world is not an end in itself but a path to what is truly intended; the Prophet likens it to a bridge to cross, not a place to build on.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r10.anchor: ومعنى هو أن الدنيا على الله سبحانه أنه تعالى لم يجعلها مقصودة لنفسه بل جعلها طريقا موصلة إلى ما هو المقصود لنفسه

BURSEVI:v9p196/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r11.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p196/r11.claim: A prophetic saying calls the world a bridge: cross it rather than settling and building there.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r11.anchor: ولذلك قال عليه السلام : الدنيا قنطرة فاعبروها لا تعمروها

BURSEVI:v9p196/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r12.speaker: بعض أهل الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v9p196/r12.claim: Some people of spiritual realization say whatever distracts a person from the Master is that person's world and a source of ill fortune.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r12.anchor: كما قال بعض أهل الحقيقة : ما ألهاك عن مولاك فهو دنياك ومشؤوم عليك

BURSEVI:v9p196/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p196/r13.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p196/r13.claim: A prophetic saying forbids reviling the world, calling it the believer's excellent mount for reaching good and escaping evil; when cursed, it answers by cursing the most disobedient to God.
BURSEVI:v9p196/r13.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : لا تسبوا الدنيا فنعمت مطية المؤمن عليها يبلغ الخير وبها ينجو من الشر

BURSEVI:v9p197/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p197/r1.claim: Repeating that God knows best reinforces the point and signals the complete divergence between the two groups He knows.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r1.anchor: تكرير قوله وهو أعلم لزيادة التقرير والإيذان بكمال تباين المعلومين

BURSEVI:v9p197/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p197/r2.claim: The persistently astray never return to guidance, while the guided are at least disposed to accept it; the opponents belong to the first class.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r2.anchor: المراد بمن ضل من أصر عليه ولم يرجع إلى الهدى أصلا وبمن اهتدى من من شأنه الاهتداء في الجملة

BURSEVI:v9p197/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p197/r3.claim: Since these people are persistently unreceptive, the Prophet should not exhaust himself by continuing to call them.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r3.anchor: فلا تتعب نفسك في دعوتهم فإنه من القبيل الأول

BURSEVI:v9p197/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p197/r4.claim: The verse alludes to the unbelieving ego and its Jewish traits: it lacks readiness for the call, and what manifests severity in pre-eternity does not manifest gentleness in eternity, and vice versa.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r4.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى النفس الكافرة ويهود صفاتها فإنهم لا يقبلون الدعوة لانتفاء استعدادهم لقبولها

BURSEVI:v9p197/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r5.speaker: الحديث القدسي
BURSEVI:v9p197/r5.claim: A sacred hadith says God created people destined for Paradise and people destined for the Fire, blessing the former and warning the latter.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث القدسي : "خلقت الجنة وخلقت لها أهلا وخلقت الناس وخلقت لها أهلا

BURSEVI:v9p197/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v9p197/r6.claim: Some great Sufis say the soul commits evil only through a companion's obstinate urging; inability to resist resembles coercion, for which law and reason do not hold one accountable.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r6.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : النفس لا تفعل الشر إلا لجاجة من القرين واللجاج ممن لا قدرة على منعه

BURSEVI:v9p197/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p197/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p197/r7.claim: The Prophet says goodness is habitual whereas evil is obstinacy; Bursevī takes this as glad tidings that the soul is good by nature and evil comes from its companion.
BURSEVI:v9p197/r7.anchor: ولذا قال عليه السلام : الخير عادة والشر لجاجة فهو بشارة عظيمة

TABATABAI:53:30-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r1.claim: The demonstrative in ‘that is their limit of knowledge’ refers to the worldly life discussed in the preceding verse.
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r1.anchor: الإشارة بذلك إلى أمر الدنيا وهو معلوم من الآية السابقة

TABATABAI:53:30-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r2.claim: The limit of their knowledge is metaphorically its endpoint: knowledge reaches the world as its object, stops there, and does not go beyond it.
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r2.anchor: من قبيل الاستعارة كأن العلم يسير إلى المعلوم وينتهي إليه وعلمهم انتهى في مسيره إلى الدنيا

TABATABAI:53:30-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r3.claim: Because their knowledge stops at worldly life, it becomes their object of desire, concern, and hope; they turn only toward it and find no reassurance beyond it.
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r3.anchor: ولازم ذلك أن تكون الدنيا متعلق إرادتهم وطلبهم

TABATABAI:53:30-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r4.claim: The assertion that God knows best who strays and who is guided confirms the preceding statement and serves as God’s testimony to it.
TABATABAI:53:30-32/r4.anchor: تأكيد لمضمون الجملة السابقة وشهادة منه تعالى عليه

TABRISI:53:26-30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:26-30/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:26-30/r6.claim: Their knowledge stops at neglecting reflection on the afterlife and pursuing immediate pleasure; this low, animal-like aim is unworthy of a rational person.
TABRISI:53:26-30/r6.anchor: منتهى علمهم وهو مبلغ خسيس لا يرضى به لنفسه عاقل

TABRISI:53:26-30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:26-30/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:26-30/r7.claim: God knows best who strays and who is guided, and will requite each according to their deeds.
TABRISI:53:26-30/r7.anchor: فيجازي كلا منهم على حسب أعمالهم

THALABI:v9p148/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r4.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v9p148/r4.claim: Al-Farra connects their limited knowledge with their claim that the angels are God’s daughters; they reach only the limits of their intellect by preferring worldly life to the Hereafter.
THALABI:v9p148/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: وذلك حين قالوا: إنهم بنات الله، تعالى الله عن افترائهم

THALABI:v9p148/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p148/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p148/r5.claim: Their knowledge ends at preferring this world to the next; the verse says God knows best who strays and who is guided.
THALABI:v9p148/r5.anchor: وازرى بهم بعد ذلك قدر عقولهم ونهاية علمهم أن آثروا الدنيا على الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says their knowledge goes no further than their belief that angels are God's daughters and will intercede for them; they rely on this and ignore the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r1.anchor: أي لم يبلغوا من العلم إلا ظنهم أن الملائكة بنات الله وأنها تشفع لهم فاعتمدوا ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq and al-Kalbi say they concern themselves only with what they need for worldly livelihood and leave the afterlife behind; al-Farra also mentions this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي إنما يعملون ما يحتاجون إليه في معايشهم، وقد نبذوا أمر الآخرة وراء ظهورهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r3.claim: God knows who strays and who is guided, and will repay each according to what they deserve.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r3.anchor: أي أنه عالم بهم فهو يجازيهم بما يستحقون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God knew the two groups before creating them, so their ultimate reward cannot escape Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p51#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد قبل أن يخلق الخلائق (¬3). والمعنى أنه أعلم بالفريقين لأنه علمهما قبل خلقهما

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r6.claim: Their knowledge reaches only this point: they have preferred this world to the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:25-30/r6.anchor: يقول: ذلك نهاية علمهم أن آثروا الدنيا على الآخرة

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r12.claim: Their knowledge reaches only the worldly life and its pleasures, as also stated in 30:7.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r12.anchor: O onların ilimden erebildikleri gaye varabildikleri son had, yani bildikleri o kadar, bütün ilimlerinin nihâyet murâdı dünyâ hayat zevkidir.

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r13.claim: God knows best those who persist in straying and those who accept guidance; this explains the command to turn away, and repeating that He knows best marks the contrast between them.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r13.anchor: Bu cümle i‘râz emrini ta‘lîldir, هُوَ أَعْلَمُ kavlinin tekrârı da her iki mâlum arasındaki tebâyünü ilandır.

ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r14.claim: Knowledge here is knowledge that orders and implements the corresponding punishment or reward.
ELMALILI:53:26-32#2/r14.anchor: “İlim”den murad da ikāb ve sevâbını tertib ve tatbik edecek vechile ilimdir.

BURHAN:v1p116/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p116/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p116/r9.claim: The parallel wording varies: al-Anʿām has من يضل and بالمهتدين; al-Qalam adds باء and past ضل; al-Najm has بمن ضل and بمن اهتدى.
BURHAN:v1p116/r9.anchor: وفى النجم ﴿ هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى ﴾

SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats ذلك مبلغهم من العلم as an interjection between the command to turn away and its reason, إن ربك.
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هو اعتراض أي: فأعرض عنه ولا تقابله، إن ربك هو أعلم

SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r2.claim: The Sheikh objects that its status as an interjection is not apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ: " كأنه يقول: هو اعتراض بين " فأعرض " وبين " إن ربك " ، ولا يظهر هذا الذي يقوله

SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r3.claim: The author replies that al-Zamakhshari explicitly links إن ربك to فأعرض as its cause; an interjection between cause and result is clear and is allowed even within a narrative.
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r3.anchor: أي: قوله: " إن ربك " علة لقوله: " فأعرض " والاعتراض بين العلة والمعلول ظاهر،

SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r4.claim: Makki allows أعلم to retain the comparative meaning, God knowing better than everyone, or to mean simply عالم, knowing.
SAMIN-DURR:53:30/r4.anchor: جوز مكي أن يكون على بابه من التفضيل أي: هو أعلم من كل أحد، بهذين الوصفين

ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r2.claim: Because they want only worldly life, their knowledge reaches only what they need for livelihood; they have cast the afterlife behind them.
ZAJJAJ:v5p74/r2.anchor: إنما يعلمون ما يحتاجون إليه في معاشهم، فقد نبذوا أمر الآخرة وراء ظهورهم

ASAD-NOTES:53:29#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:29#n22/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:29#n22/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase as the total extent or goal of their knowledge.
ASAD-NOTES:53:29#n22/r1.anchor: Lit., "that is their sum-total [or "goal"] of knowledge".

ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r1.claim: That most naturally refers to worldly life understood from context; other suggestions are their turning away or conjectures, which Alusi rejects.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r1.anchor: ذكر اسم الإشارة وقيل : أي ما أداهم إلى ما هم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r2.claim: Their limit of knowledge is its furthest extent; knowledge includes false conjecture and the plural pronoun refers to the group by sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r2.anchor: ( مبلغهم من العلم ( أي منتهى علمهم لا علم لهم فوقه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r3.claim: The statement confirms that their desire is confined to worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r3.anchor: واعتراض مقررلمضمون ما قبلها من قصر الإرادة على الحياة الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r4.claim: The pronoun is plural by meaning, whereas the earlier singular follows the word's form.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r4.anchor: وضمير ( مبلغهم ) لمن وجمع باعتبار معناه كما أن إفراده قبل باعتبار لفظه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r5.claim: The statement explains the command to turn away; repeating He knows intensifies confirmation and warns through contrasting groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r5.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالأعراض وتكرير قوله تعالى : ( هو أعلم ) لزيادة التقرير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r6.claim: Those astray never turn back, while the guided can accept guidance; do not exhaust yourself trying to win over the first group.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p60#2/r6.anchor: والمراد ( بمن ضل ) من أصر على الضلال ولم يرجع إلى الهدى أصلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r6.claim: Their knowledge and intellectual capacity end at preferring worldly life over the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r6.anchor: أي: ذلك نهاية علمهم وقدر عقولهم أن آثروا الدنيا على الآخرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r7.claim: Another view says they know only conjectures that angels are God's daughters and will intercede, on which they rely while turning away from the Quran.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p410#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: لم يبلغوا من العلم إلا ظنهم أن الملائكة بنات الله، وأنها تشفع لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p411/r1.claim: God knows both groups, those astray and those guided, and will recompense them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r1.claim: Turn away from calling and concerning yourself with one who neglects God, pursues worldly life as his sole aim, and becomes more obstinate when invited.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r1.anchor: فأعرض عن دعوته والاهتمام بشأنه فإن من غفل عن الله وأعرض عن ذكره

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r2.claim: Dhālika may refer to worldly affairs or their desirability; their knowledge goes no further than that.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r3.claim: This parenthetical statement reinforces that their aspirations are confined to worldly life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r3.anchor: لا يتجاوزه علمهم والجملة اعتراض مقرر

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r4.claim: God knows who will respond and who will not; this explains the command to turn away, since the Messenger's duty is to convey and he has done so.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:30-31/r4.anchor: إنما يعلم الله من يجيب ممن لا يجيب فلا تتعب نفسك في دعوتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r3.claim: “That is their reach of knowledge” is sarcastic: they have no real knowledge because their inner sight is blind and darkened to the afterlife, the root of all knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r3.anchor: وتهكم بهم بقوله : { من العلم } أنه لا علم لهم لأن عيون بصائرهم عمي , ومرائبها كثيفة مظلمة لا تكشف عن نظر الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r4.claim: God alone knows who remains astray and who is guided; the Prophet should not expect worldly knowledge or forceful admonition to reveal or determine their ultimate state.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r4.anchor: إن ربك } أي المحسن إليك بالإرسال وغيره { هو } أي وحده { أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله } ضلالا مستمرا , فلا تعلق أملك بأن يصل علمه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r5.claim: Calling God “your Lord” signals that the astray person’s exclusion may itself benefit the Prophet: had he joined the faith, he might have corrupted more than he improved.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r5.anchor: وعبر بالرب إارة إلى أن ضلال هذا من الإحسان إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه لودخل في دنيه لأفسد أكثر مما يصلح

BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r6.speaker: مصعب بن عمير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r6.claim: The source gives Musʿab’s preaching as an example of counsel blessed by God: Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh accepted Islam within one hour.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p326/r6.anchor: كما فعل في وعظ مصعب بن عمير رضي الله عنه فصغى له أسيد بن حضير وسعد بن معاذ رضي الله عنهما في ساعة واحدة

IBNHIBBAN:6585/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says one should report only what one knows and that admitting ignorance is itself knowledge; he cites the Prophet's refusal to be among the pretentious.
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r1.anchor: فأتيت ابن مسعود، قال: وكان متكئا، فغضب، فجلس، وقال: يا أيها الناس من علم شيئا

IBNHIBBAN:6585/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r2.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the smoke verses with Quraysh's famine after the Prophet prayed for seven lean years: they saw smoke, Abu Sufyan sought relief, the punishment lifted, and they returned to disbelief.
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r2.anchor: فأتيت ابن مسعود، قال: وكان متكئا، فغضب، فجلس، وقال: يا أيها الناس من علم شيئا

IBNHIBBAN:6585/r3.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r3.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the great seizure and the promised binding punishment with Badr, and says the Roman episode and four events had passed.
IBNHIBBAN:6585/r3.anchor: فأتيت ابن مسعود، قال: وكان متكئا، فغضب، فجلس، وقال: يا أيها الناس من علم شيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r1.claim: Since their misguidance resulted from turning away from God's reminder, the Prophet is told to turn away from them; the audience is those rejecting the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r1.anchor: بعد أن وصف مداركهم الباطلة وضلالهم فرع عليه أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بالإعراض عنهم ذلك لأن ما تقدم من وصف ضلالهم كان نتيجة إعراضهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r9.claim: The referent is plural, but the verb is singular to agree with man; the plural suffix in ‘their limit’ confirms the plural referent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p116/r9.anchor: وما صدق { من تولى } القوم الذين تولوا وإنما جرى الفعل على صيغة المفرد مراعاة للفظ { من }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r4.claim: The clause parenthetically explains their ignorance of the afterlife, belittling their limited understanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r4.anchor: وجملة { ذلك مبلغهم من العلم } اعتراض وهو استئناف بياني بين به سبب جهلهم بوجود الحياة الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r5.claim: This explanatory parenthesis interrupts the preceding clauses and their cause, which follows in ‘Your Lord knows best who strayed.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p117/r5.anchor: وهذا الاستئناف وقع معترضا بين الجمل وعلتها في قوله : { إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r1.claim: ‘That’ points to their wanting only worldly life and metaphorically marks the limit reached by a traveler unable to know beyond it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ذلك } إشارة إلى المذكور في الكلام السابق من قوله : { ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r2.claim: God's knowledge grounds the command to turn away and consoles the Prophet; it implies God will reckon with and requite the misguided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r2.anchor: تعليل لجملة { فأعرض عن من تولى } وهو تسلية للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم والخبر مستعمل في معنى أنه متولي حسابهم وجزائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r3.claim: Inna and the separating pronoun emphasize the implied reckoning, not God's bare omniscience; God knows their condition better than the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r3.anchor: والتوكيد المفاد ب { إن } وبضمير الفصل راجع إلى المعنى الكنائي ، وأما كونه تعالى أعلم بذلك فلا مقتضى لتأكيدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r4.claim: The separating pronoun expresses real restriction: the Prophet does not know their inner states and should not grieve over them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r4.anchor: وضمير الفصل مفيد القصر وهو قصر حقيقي . والمعنى : أنت لا تعلم دخائلهم فلا تتحسر عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r5.claim: The addition about the rightly guided completes the point, promising believers and reassuring the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r5.anchor: وجملة { وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى } تتميم ، وفيه وعد للمؤمنين وبشارة للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r6.claim: Bi governs both forms of aʿlam and marks association with the straying or guided person's state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r6.anchor: والباء في ب { من ضل } وفي ب { من اهتدى } لتعدية صفتي { أعلم } وهي للملابسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r7.claim: The straying precede the guided because they matter more here; the latter complete the statement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p118/r7.anchor: وتقديم ذكر { من ضل } على ذكر { من اهتدى } لأن الضالين أهم في هذا المقام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r7.claim: Their knowledge reaches only worldly matters such as farming, crafts, and seeking status through deception, not useful knowledge of the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r7.anchor: انتهى تحصيلهم من المعلومات، وذلك أن المعلومات منها ما هي معقولات نافعة في الآخرة، ومنها ما هي أمور فانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r8.claim: The statement continues the consolation in the command to turn away, warns unbelievers, and promises believers reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r8.anchor: الآية تصل بمعنى التسلية في قوله: فأعرض عن من تولى عن ذكرنا، وقوله: إن ربك هو أعلم الآية، ووعيد للكفار ووعد للمؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r9.claim: Misguidance and guidance are attributed to people through acquisition, although both are created and originated by God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p202#3/r9.anchor: وأسند الضلالة والهدى إليهم بكسبهم وإن كان الجميع خلقا له واختراعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says their knowledge reaches only what they need for worldly livelihoods; they have cast aside the matter of the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج إنما يعلمون ما يحتاجون إليه في معايشهم وقد نبذوا أمر الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p75#2/r2.claim: God knows both groups—the astray and the guided—and will recompense them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r5.claim: The rejecter seeks only worldly life; its pursuit is the full extent of his ambition and knowledge, which is why it is called their limit of knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r5.anchor: أي: وإنما (2) أكثر (3) همه ومبلغ علمه الدنيا، فذاك هو غاية ما لا خير فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r6.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r6.claim: Aisha reports the saying that the world is a home for the homeless and wealth for the penniless, gathered by one without intelligence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r6.anchor: وقد روى الإمام أحمد عن أم المؤمنين عائشة [رضي الله عنها] (5) قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الدنيا دار من لا دار له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r7.speaker: الدعاء المأثور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r7.claim: A transmitted supplication asks God not to make worldly life the greatest concern or limit of one's knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459/r7.anchor: وفي الدعاء المأثور: "اللهم لا تجعل الدنيا أكبر همنا، ولا مبلغ علمنا".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.claim: God creates all creatures, knows what benefits His servants, guides and misguides whom He wills through power, knowledge, and wisdom, and is always just in both law and decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p459#2/r1.anchor: أي: هو الخالق لجميع المخلوقات، والعالم بمصالح عباده، وهو الذي يهدي من يشاء، ويضل من يشاء، وذلك كله عن قدرته وعلمه وحكمته

JISHUMI:v9p6651/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6651/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6651/r13.claim: This is their limit of knowledge: preferring transient worldly life, or knowing worldly benefit but not the afterlife's lasting reward, which they abandon in ignorance.
JISHUMI:v9p6651/r13.anchor: ذلك مبلغهم من العلم أي: نهاية قدر علمهم، حيث آثروا الدنيا الفانية على الآخرة، وقيل: علمهم انتهى إلى نفع الدنيا دون نفع الآخرة

JISHUMI:v9p6651/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6651/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6651/r14.claim: God knows who strays from His religion and who is guided, and rewards each according to deeds.
JISHUMI:v9p6651/r14.anchor: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله أي: دينه وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى فيجازي كل أحد بحسب عمله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r5.claim: God knows who responds; the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves, and his duty is only to convey the message.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r5.anchor: إنما يعلم الله من يجيب ممن لا يجيب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r6.claim: ذلك مبلغهم من العلم is parenthetical or attached to the command to turn away; God knows the misguided and guided and will repay each as deserved.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p425#2/r6.anchor: اعتراض أو فأعرض عنه ولا تقابله

MUJAHID:v2p631/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p631/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p631/r1.claim: Mujahid explains this as the limit of their opinion.
MUJAHID:v2p631/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ذلك مبلغهم من العلم ﴾ يعني مبلغ رأيهم

MUQATIL:53:27-30/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:27-30/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:27-30/r5.claim: Their knowledge reaches only the claims that angels are female and will intercede for them.
MUQATIL:53:27-30/r5.anchor: يعني من مبلغ رأيهم من العلم أن الملائكة إناث وأنها تشفع لهم

MUQATIL:53:27-30/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:27-30/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:27-30/r6.claim: God knows who strays from guidance and who is guided, and He is independent of their worship; angels and all others are His servants and possessions.
MUQATIL:53:27-30/r6.anchor: ثم عظم نفسه بأنه غني عن عبادتهم والملائكة وغيرهم عبيده وفي ملكه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r1.claim: “That” refers to their choosing and being satisfied with this worldly life; that is the limit of their knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ اى اختيارهم النيا والرضا بها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r2.claim: Allah knows who is astray and who is guided, and will requite each.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p190#7/r2.anchor: اى هو اعلم بالضال والمهتدى ومجازيهما

QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r8.claim: Their knowledge reaches worldly affairs, while they remain ignorant about religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r8.anchor: إنما يبصرون أمر دنياهم ويجهلون أمر دينهم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r9.claim: Al-Farra says this belittles them: choosing this world over the next marks the limit of their intellect and knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: صغرهم وازدرى بهم أي ذلك قدر عقولهم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r10.claim: Another view says their limited knowledge is their claim that angels and idols are God's daughters.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r10.anchor: وقيل: أن جعلوا الملائكة والأصنام بنات الله

QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r11.claim: God knows who strayed from His religion and who is guided, and recompenses each according to deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:27-30/r11.anchor: أي حاد عن دينه { وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى }
